title: EGY-05 · The future with ḥa-: projects, invitations, appointments

blocks.text: EGY-05 · The future with ḥa-: projects, invitations, appointments
Lesson overview

With the present (EGY-03) and the past (EGY-04) tales; with the future organize. In Egyptian the future is very simple: ḥa- in front of the imperfect (ḥaktib (I shall write to the House) miš (miš ḥaktib). In this unit you use it to make projects, invite, accept and refuse with politeness, set an appointment: the situations that you will live every day in Cairo, and that prepare Luke's arrival in July. Six weeks, in parallel with B1-12, B1-13 and B1-14.

rows: 8–9 hours · six weeks (weeks 119–124), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, a tutor or Egyptian conversation partner, tutor recordings on the phone
Targets. At the end of the unit you know:
1. to form and deny the future with ḥa- and miš ḥa-;
2. expressing intentions (nāwi) and plans;
3. invite, accept and refuse in a courteous manner;
4. set a place, day and time for an appointment, and move it;
5. use future expressions of time (bukra, baʿd bukra, il-usbūʿ ig-gayy, kamān šuwayya).
Six-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week).

2. The Egyptian future and the fuṣḥā
⁧لَنْ أُسَافِرَ⁩ miš ḥasāfir I won't leave.

ḥa- or has-? Cairo feels like it. ḥa- is ha- (with light h), especially in the fast talk: haktib, hanrūḥ. They're the same thing; in this course we write ḥa-. Future and present. As in English, the present with b- can indicate a near and planned future: bukra barūḥ il-gamʿa I'm going to college tomorrow. ḥa- stresses the intention or prediction.
3. Conjugation and Denial
The future is formed by ḥa- + simple imperfect (without b-).

Denial Is Always miš : miš ḥaktib I won't write, miš ḥanrūḥ We're not going. Never but...-š with the future. With the pronouns: ḥaʾullak I'll tell you, ḥašufak Bukra ... I see you tomorrow... ḥakallimha I'll call her.

5. Invite, accept, reject

rows: tīgi maʿāna? · ēh raʾyak nitʿašša Sawa? · ana ʿāzmak ʿala ʾahwa
Are you coming with us? · How about dinner together? · I offer you a coffee
Let's go! · Why don't you come...
All right · Perfect · With pleasure · Sure!
maʿlišš, miš ḥaʾdar · ʿandi mišwār · marra tanya in šāʾ allāh
I'm sorry, I can't · I have a commitment · Another time, if God wills

blocks.text: thank you mutašakkir ʾawi · tislam Thank you very much · Thank you for the invitation to refuse in Egypt. A dry "no" is rude. Thanks, you give a reason (also vague: ʿandi mišwār I have a commission to do and it opens up to another occasion (marra tanya). Often a first refusal is part of the courtesy, and he who invites insists: lāzimYou must! ʿazam / ʿāzim Invite, offer... ʿāzmak I'll buy it. The inviter usually pays.
6. Setting up an appointment

rows: When do I see you? · Where do we see each other?
All right, I'll see you at the appointment.
Can we reschedule until the day after tomorrow?

blocks.text: warning a delay ḥatʾaḫḫar ʿašar daʾāyiʾ, maʿlišš I'm ten minutes late.

maʿād • appointment (fuṣḥā ⁧مَوْعِد⁩ ). ʿala l-maʿād (a) punctual; the appointment is not possible. The Egyptian weather is more elastic than the Italian one, but for work appointments and trains punctuality counts.

9. Pronunciation

The prefix ḥa-. ḥa-aktib contract in ḥaktib; ḥa-yiktib in ḥayiktib. Exercise with the tutor alternating present and future: baktib / ḥaktib, biyrūḥ / ḥayrūḥ, binākul / ḥanākul. The pitch of the invitations. An Egyptian invitation has a warm and insistent tone: tīgi maʿāna? It goes up a lot in the end. Imitalo: a flat-tone invitation sounds untrue.

★ ⁧الجاي⁩ ig-gayy · ig-next, next ⁧القَادِم⁩ adjective il-usbūʿ ig-gayy gayya

miš ḥaʾdar I won't be able to do that.

blocks.text: Notes.gāb is carried in the sense of taking and carrying: gibli mayya For carrying with you it is also used ḫad maʿā. fāḍi also applies to empty: il-ʾahwa faḍya The bar is empty. ʾidir in the present baʾdar, biyiʾdar; to the future ḥaʾdar: miš ḥaʾdar aḥḍar I won't be able to come.

Exercise 6 · Projects

Listen to Script B and write for each message: who calls · what he proposes or announces · when · what answer he needs.
12. Listening
Egyptian scripts should be read by an Egyptian speaker (tutor, tandem partner): vocal synthesis does not pronounce the dialect reliably.
Script A · Dialogues 1 and 2
The reader reads the dialogues at normal speed. Listen without reading, then answer questions a) and b) for the year 8.
Script B · Three voice messages
⁧١. أهلًا يا لوكا، أنا مينا. هسافر يوم الحد الصبح. لو فاضي بكرة بالليل، تعالى نشرب قهوة. كلمني.⁩

⁧٣. يا لوكا، أنا شريف. معلش، مش هقدر أجي المطار يوم تلاتة، عندي مشوار مع خالي. بس ياسمين⁩

17. To switch to the next unit

Switch to EGY-06 if you have at least 16/20 and if in the role play of invitations (oral production 2) you have refused with grace, without a dry "no" . In EGY-06 learn the imperative and ask and from directions, and move with taxi, metro and microbus.
